text.p: Rodamco NV said on Friday it expected net earnings per share to rise by more than 20 percent in the financial year to February 28, 1998.
"The management board now expects a rise of more than 20 percent to a level of about 3.40 guilders (per share)," the property arm of the Robeco group of investment funds said.
Last December Rodamco said it expected earnings per share to rise by about 10 percent in 1997/98.

Earlier on Friday, Rodamco posted a provisional 1996/97 net profit of 447 million guilders compared with 446 million in the previous year. Net per share grew fractionally to 2.81 guilders from 2.80, the first time since 1990/91 net earnings per share did not fall.
The figure was better than expected. Rodamco said on previous occasions it expected a slight profit fall in 1996/97.

Results were positively affected by higher rental income, a gradual recovery of the international property markets and by clearly positive currency rate gains on the U.S. dollar and the pound sterling in particular, it said.
Rodamco said its net earnings per share in the second half of 1996/97 were 16 percent higher than in the first half.

Rodamco wants to pay an unchanged dividend of 2.80 guilders per share. As in previous years, shareholders can also opt for a payment in shares which is tax-exempt for private Dutch investors. The full dividend proposal will be published in May.

Last year, all shares issued as stock dividend were subsequently bought back by Rodamco. This had a favourable effect of 0.09 guilders on the net earnings per share, it said. Rodamco said it was also prepared to buy back its own shares in 1997/98.
This would depend on the difference between the share price and net asset value per share, developments in interest rates and investment opportunities.
"As in the previous year, the company will not repurchase more shares than will be issued as stock dividend within the framework of the optional dividend in July 1997," Rodamco said.
